theme_central: Exclusive devotion to Allah (ikhlas) as the remedy for arrogance — culminating in the most hope-filled verse of the Qur'an: never despair of Allah's mercy.
sources_note: Precisely sourced division (grokipedia, thelastdialogue.org): 1-8, 9-20, 21-31, 32-47. Continuation (48-75) reconstructed from the well-known key verse 39:53 and the final scene of the "zumar" (groups) that gives the surah its name.

branches.title: Monotheism and prophethood
branches.resume: Pure and sincere religion belongs to Allah; creation of man in stages in the mother's womb.

children.t: Pure religion belongs to Allah, creation of man in stages

branches.title: Consolation, steadfastness
branches.resume: He who worships with devotion at night is not equal to the heedless; command to remain steadfast and sincere.

children.t: The night worshipper is not equal to the heedless; sincerity required

branches.title: Contrast: sincere believers / the heedless
branches.resume: Water irrigating the earth as a parable, contrast between a breast opened to Islam and a hardened heart.

children.t: Parable of water irrigating the earth, breast opened to Islam vs hardened heart

branches.title: Refutation of shirk
branches.resume: Who is more unjust than the one who lies about Allah? Allah suffices for His servant.

children.t: Refutation of shirk, Allah suffices for His servant

branches.title: The verse of hope
branches.resume: Fate at the Judgment, then the most hope-filled verse in the Qur'an: never despair of mercy.

children.t: Fate of the transgressors, expansion or restriction of sustenance
"Do not despair of Allah's mercy" — He forgives all sins

branches.title: Closing: the groups (zumar)
branches.resume: Source of the surah's name: disbelievers and believers led in groups toward Hell and Paradise.

children.t: Blackened faces of the liars, exclusive call to worship Allah
The groups (zumar) led toward Hell and Paradise, the Throne surrounded by angels
